title: Python Virtual Environments
definition: Python's ability to create isolated environments for software development, allowing different projects to have their own unique set of dependencies.

difficulty_levels.beginner: A Python virtual environment is like a separate room for your project. It has its own space and tools, so it doesn't interfere with other projects.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A Python virtual environment is a feature that creates an isolated Python environment for each project. This is done by creating a folder which contains a Python executable file, which points to a copy of the Python standard library.
difficulty_levels.expert: Python virtual environments challenge the traditional view of software development, which often leads to dependency conflicts between projects. This concept connects software engineering with system administration, and it has implications for understanding the nature of complexity and scalability.

extra_fields.insight: The ability to create isolated environments can lead to more efficient and scalable software development.
